name: Shortest integer Golomb ruler with 29 marks
compute_profile: laptop-hours for initial construction searches. The cost of proving optimality is unknown.
statement: A Golomb ruler with 29 marks is a sequence of integers 0 = a_1 < a_2 < ... < a_29 whose 406 positive pairwise differences are distinct. Its length is a_29. Let G(29) be the minimum length. The distributed.net OGR project established G(28) = 585. The two end gaps of a 29-mark ruler are distinct positive integers, so at least one is at least two. Deleting the endpoint adjacent to that gap leaves a 28-mark ruler of length at least 585, giving G(29) >= 587. James B. Shearer credits the 623 construction to Atkinson and Hassenklover, and Tomas Rokicki and Gil Dogon publish a 623 ruler in their data. The checked interval is 587 <= G(29) <= 623, with the exact value open. FormalMarket accepts submissions of 29-mark rulers of length at most 622. Few Shots tracks the same record and lists length 623.
success_criterion: Determine G(29). Give a 29-mark ruler of length L and an independently checkable proof excluding all such rulers of length at most L - 1. At L = 587 the lower-bound argument in the statement suffices. Before claiming, recheck OEIS A003022, distributed.net/OGR, the two challenge pages, public ruler archives, and later literature to confirm G(29) remains unsettled at claim time.

partial_wins.statement: Give a 29-mark ruler of length at most 622 that is strictly shorter than the best public 29-mark ruler at claim time.
Certify a lower bound on G(29) of at least 588 that strictly improves the strongest comparable public lower bound at claim time.

verification_method: Check that the witness has 29 distinct integer marks. Sort them, subtract the smallest mark, and verify the length and all 406 positive pairwise differences. Calibrate on the 28-mark length-585 and 29-mark length-623 records in Rokicki and Dogon's ruler archive, and reject a control with a repeated difference. To certify a lower bound B, independently regenerate a SAT encoding of normalized increasing marks 0 = a_1 < a_2 < ... < a_29 <= B - 1 with all 406 positive pairwise differences distinct, then check a DRAT or LRAT refutation. Reflection symmetry breaking (a_2 - a_1 < a_29 - a_28) preserves a representative of every valid ruler because end gaps are distinct. Prove that any additional symmetry restrictions preserve a representative of every feasible ruler. A kernel-checked mathematical exclusion also qualifies. Certificates exceeding 1 MB follow kit/SUBMIT.md section 1.
angles: Use the earlier optimal lengths to bound the spans of consecutive groups of marks. For construction searches, keep counts of pairwise differences and update the counts when moving a mark.
pitfalls: OEIS A003022 gives proved minima and stops at 28 marks. Shearer's table and the Rokicki-Dogon archive give the construction bound 623 at 29 marks.
Weaker upper bounds reported in recent preprints (such as 757) do not supersede the 1984 Atkinson-Hassenklover length-623 construction.
OEIS A036501 (number of inequivalent optimal rulers) stops at 19 marks, so uniqueness of length 585 at 28 marks is not established in OEIS; proving G(29) >= 588 is therefore nontrivial.
A lower-bound certificate must cover every ruler within its length limit, including rulers that do not come from modular constructions.
The search is for integer marks on a line. Check ordinary positive differences between marks.
